desc: Sort arrays A, B, and C in descending order.
Determine the cutoff index $M$ such that $M^3 \ge K$ (e.g., $M = \lceil K^{1/3} \rceil$).
Extract the top $M$ elements from each sorted array to form smaller arrays $A', B', C'$.
Generate all $M^3$ possible values of $A'_i B'_j + B'_j C'_k + C'_k A'_i$.
Sort these generated values in descending order and output the $K$-th element (index $K-1$).
Ensure to handle the case where $K > M^3$ (though by definition $M^3 \ge K$, so this won't happen if $M$ is chosen correctly).
Implement the solution in Python: read inputs, sort arrays, determine cutoff $M$, generate top $M^3$ values, sort, and print the $K$-th largest.
Run the code against Sample 1, Sample 2, and Sample 3 to verify correctness.
If any sample fails, debug and fix.
If all pass, mark as solved.
